questions.text: A book is resting on a table and not moving. What is true about the forces on it?
options: Only one force pushes on it
There are no forces at all
questions.explanation: When an object stays still, the forces on it are balanced. Gravity pulls down and the table pushes up with equal force.

questions.text: Two teams pull on a rope in a tug of war. The rope suddenly moves to the left. What does this tell you?
options: The left team pulled with more force
questions.explanation: The rope moves toward the stronger pull. An unbalanced force, with more pull on the left, made the rope move left.

questions.text: A swing goes back and forth in a regular way. Because this motion has a pattern, you can do what?
options: Predict where it will go next
Never know where it will be
questions.explanation: When motion follows a regular pattern, you can predict its future motion. The swing repeats the same path.

questions.text: You hold two magnets near each other and feel a push WITHOUT them touching. What causes this?
questions.explanation: Magnets can push or pull each other without touching. This is a magnetic force that acts across a distance.

questions.text: Two magnets are brought together and they PUSH apart. This means the poles facing each other are:
questions.explanation: Like poles (north-north or south-south) push apart, or repel. Opposite poles pull together, or attract.

questions.text: A refrigerator magnet sticks to a metal door. Which object would a magnet also stick to?
questions.explanation: Magnets attract certain metals like steel. A steel paperclip will stick, but plastic, wood, and paper will not.

questions.text: Which shows the correct order of a butterfly's life cycle?
questions.explanation: A butterfly's life cycle goes egg, then caterpillar, then chrysalis, then adult butterfly. Living things have life cycles.

questions.text: Why do many animals, like wolves, live together in groups?
options: Groups help them hunt and stay safe
questions.explanation: Living in a group helps animals find food, hunt, and protect one another from danger.

questions.text: A tall plant makes seeds that grow into new plants. The new plants are most likely to be:
questions.explanation: Offspring inherit traits from their parents. Tall plants tend to produce plants that are also tall, though there is some variation.

questions.text: A puppy learns a trick from training. This trait comes from:
questions.explanation: Some traits are influenced by the environment. A learned trick comes from training and experience, not from inheritance.

questions.text: Scientists find a fossil of a fish inside a rock on a dry mountain. What can they conclude?
questions.explanation: Fossils are clues about the past. A fish fossil on a mountain shows that the area was once covered by water long ago.

questions.text: In a herd of deer, the fastest deer are best at escaping wolves. Over time, what is most likely?
options: More deer in the herd will be fast
The deer will turn into wolves
questions.explanation: Traits that help animals survive are passed on more often. Fast deer survive to have young, so more of the herd becomes fast.

questions.text: A polar bear has thick fur and lives in a very cold place. Where would it struggle the MOST to survive?
questions.explanation: Living things survive well in habitats that match their needs. A polar bear's thick fur would make a hot desert very hard to survive in.

questions.text: Weather reporters keep records of temperature each day for a season. Why?
options: To describe typical weather and see patterns
questions.explanation: Recording weather over time shows patterns and helps describe the typical weather, or climate, of a season.

questions.text: A place near the equator is usually hot all year. This describes the area's:
questions.explanation: Climate is the pattern of weather in a place over many years. Areas near the equator have a hot climate.

questions.text: A town is often hit by strong winds. Which design would best reduce damage to a house?
options: Making the roof out of leaves
questions.explanation: Engineers reduce weather damage with strong designs. Strong, well-secured roofs help a house survive high winds.

questions.text: Before designing a solution, engineers should clearly know the:
options: Problem and what a good solution needs to do
questions.explanation: A good design starts with defining the problem and the criteria, or what the solution must do to succeed.

questions.text: You test three paper cup designs to see which holds the most water without leaking. Testing helps you:
questions.explanation: Fair tests let engineers compare designs and find which parts work best, so they can improve the solution.
